question: Does avoiding the existing decimal-string roundtrip for exactly integral TYPE_FLOAT values in [-1024,1024] remove a real remaining continuation cost without changing any policy or game result?
rationale: The completed profile attributes about 60 percent of root time to greedy continuation. The current qualified ji fast path handles TYPE_INT only. First establish actual content types; do not assume a workload benefit.
allowed_change: One ji conversion branch only: TYPE_FLOAT, bounded range, and exact equality to its integer conversion. Preserve the existing TYPE_INT branch. All other values execute the existing fallback unchanged. No tolerance, different score, cache lifecycle, parameters, content, acquisition or random law.

numeric_proof.exhaustive_domain: Every one of the 2049 integral binary64 values -1024 through 1024, plus signed zero; compare to the original native int(float(str(v))) operation.
numeric_proof.fallbacks: Adjacent fractional and out-of-range values, large integers, strings, StringName, booleans and null retain the reference result. Unsafe unconditional cast must be detected by known counterexamples.
numeric_proof.real_input_measurement: Count numeric Variant types and guarded-branch eligibility in parsed pinned content; report descriptive counts only.
numeric_proof.stop: Any equality failure or lack of relevant integral float inputs stops promotion; preserve the actual failure. A parser or delivery defect is not a scientific zero.

conditional_workload_benchmark.entry: Only after numeric equivalence and source-only scope tests pass.
conditional_workload_benchmark.selection: First cell of each index quartile, selected by assignment rather than outcome or timing.
conditional_workload_benchmark.reference: Existing safe-integer continuation implementation, not a weaker controller.
conditional_workload_benchmark.acceptance: Every full native trace and every endpoint/decision/score field equals the preserved original, excluding only already designated top-level timing counters. Both repetition aggregate refined/reference CPU ratios <=0.90; no per-cell ratio above1.05. No timing-based candidate selection.
conditional_workload_benchmark.limits: A microbenchmark is not full-workload cost qualification. The old 4015.74 and3729.33-second terminals remain immutable. The3600-second whole-method/vow limit is unchanged. No support aggregation or V0 may open from these timings.

preservation: Commit source before native measurements; preserve all available stdout/stderr, commands, raw and manifests; obtain a separate remote byte readback. Never replace old captures.
